_status: The 15 §G / 20 §6 register: one row per generation tool, and whether its commercial terms
🔒 `confirmedInWriting` is ABSENT on every row below, and absent means UNSET — nobody has
confirmed anything. There was no default: the (since removed) provenance gate read an absent member as null,
ToolLicence.RequireConfirmedInWriting() throws on it, and ProvenanceGate raises
UnconfirmedLicence for any asset whose record names the tool. The day the first Midjourney
asset is delivered, this file is what decides whether the build is green.
⛔ FILLING THIS IN IS M8-01b AND THE PRODUCT OWNER OWNS IT. Confirming a licence is a legal
act, not an engineering task; no agent may set `confirmedInWriting`. A `true` also requires a
`confirmationRef` naming where the written confirmation is filed — 15 §G calls the bare claim
a formality, and a formality is what this register exists to refuse.
Adding a row is not the same as licensing a tool. A row with no confirmation still fails the
gate; what a row buys is that the failure says 'not confirmed' rather than 'never heard of it'.

licences.note: 15 §B0 🔒 locks Midjourney as the art tool and states that commercial rights are included on paid plans. M8 kickoff 2026-08-12: the paid plan IS held. §G's separate requirement — confirm the current commercial terms in writing before the first batch — is M8-01b and is NOT DONE. `confirmedInWriting` stays absent until it is.

$notListed: Suno, Udio and ElevenLabs are NOT rows here, deliberately. M8 kickoff 2026-08-12: no licence
is held for any of them, and 20 §2.1 says to check the terms BEFORE generating anything. All
106 audio assets are blocked on licence and on capability alike. A row with no confirmation
would still fail the gate, so adding one would change nothing about what may be generated —
but it would read as a shortlist somebody had decided on, and nobody has.
Procedural output names no tool at all: its 'tool' is this repository, which needs no
commercial licence. A CC0 pack names none either — its terms travel on the record, in the
`licence` member, which is what a CC0 dedication is.
